title: The Danger of Back-Pitched Waste Pipes
description: A common mistake in drainage installation is allowing horizontal waste pipes to back-pitch, sloping upward toward the main drain instead of downward. When a waste pipe lacks proper fall, water pools in low spots rather than carrying waste efficiently. Over time, heavy organic solids settle at the bottom while liquid flows over them, resulting in recurring blockages and standing wastewater inside the pipe. Proper pitch relies on a continuous downward grade to maintain flow velocity, preventing solids from separating. Always verify slope using a level before permanently securing pipe hangers and straps.

The Danger of Back-Pitched Waste Pipes

A common mistake in drainage installation is allowing horizontal waste pipes to back-pitch, sloping upward toward the main drain instead of downward. When a waste pipe lacks proper fall, water pools in low spots rather than carrying waste efficiently. Over time, heavy organic solids settle at the bottom while liquid flows over them, resulting in recurring blockages and standing wastewater inside the pipe. Proper pitch relies on a continuous downward grade to maintain flow velocity, preventing solids from separating. Always verify slope using a level before permanently securing pipe hangers and straps.
